title: Should Remodelers Use Voice AI on Real-Time Leads or Aged Leads?
summary: Testing voice AI on old leads feels safe, but it hides what AI does best. Here's why remodelers should start with real-time leads and how to run a fair test.
body_markdown:
By[Pam Torrey](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pam-torrey-920175b4/) , Senior Director of Marketing at Leaping AI


When a remodeler decides to bring voice AI into their business, the “safe” first move is always the same. They begin by testing it on old leads.


That makes sense if you’re looking from a cost-conscious perspective. Old leads feel like gambling with house money. Nobody on the team is working them anymore so if the AI makes a mistake, nothing is lost. And, if it actually books a few appointments off a list you weren't planning to work anyway, great!


The problem is what you’re measuring with that test. Leads that are over two weeks old have already gone quiet. Some homeowners booked with another contractor. Some decided not to go through with the project. Some were just shopping around and ended up on a lead list. If you put any rep on that list, human or AI, the numbers aren’t going to be great.


So the test comes back with underwhelming results and the conclusion is, “AI doesn’t set as many appointments as our human call center reps.” That is fundamentally the wrong lesson. The test was set up around the one place voice AI has the least room to win.


Voice AI does its best work in the first few minutes after a lead comes in, and in the days of immediate follow-up after that. It’s where most remodelers should start with voice AI agents. Here’s why, and how to run a test that will give you real results.


## **A lead at minute one and a lead at day 14 are different people**


Put yourself in the position of a homeowner who just filled out a form for a new walk-in shower. Right now, they’re thinking about their bathroom, and how it doesn’t fit their lifestyle, family, or home anymore. Their phone is in hand. They might have filled out two or three forms requesting information in the last ten minutes.


The company that calls first has a real chance at the project. The company that calls 24 hours later or on the next business day is calling someone who already has an in-home consultation on the calendar with someone else.


This isn't a new concept. Researchers writing in[Harvard Business Review](https://hbr.org/2011/03/the-short-life-of-online-sales-leads) studied how fast companies follow up on web leads and found that most companies are not responding nearly fast enough. The same is true on the phone.[CallRail reports](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250114793850/en/CallRail-Releases-Report-Benchmarking-Marketing-Efforts-for-Small-Businesses) that up to 85% of callers whose calls go unanswered won't call back.


Now, fast-forward two weeks for that same homeowner. They’ve either booked an appointment, moved on, or stopped picking up unknown numbers. It’s still possible to reach that homeowner, and it’s worth the try, but it’s a different job and you should expect different results.


That’s why an aged-lead test makes a rough first impression. You’re judging a tool based on working the hardest leads in your CRM, leaving out the leads where the speed and consistency of AI do most of the work.


## **Where voice AI does its best work**


The best call center rep can only handle one lead at a time. That’s just the reality of the role. When ten leads hit at 10:15am on a Tuesday and your call center only has four reps on, some of those leads will have to wait. When a lead comes in during lunch, or your team is juggling confirm calls plus inbound leads, they may have to wait even longer.


Voice AI agents don’t wait. A lead comes in from a form fill, a lead aggregator, or an inbound call and it gets touched right away. A strong speed-to-lead setup will look like this:


1.


A text goes out the moment the lead arrives, so the homeowner knows who's reaching out.


2.


The voice agent calls right after.


3.


If there's no answer, it calls again right away. Because plenty of homeowners let an unknown number ring out once, a quick second call gives them another chance to pick up.


All of it happens inside your contact hours, in the homeowner's local time.


[Lifetime Bath & Glass](https://leapingai.com/customers/appointment-booking-with-voice-ai-lifetime-bath) buys leads from multiple vendors and was getting beaten to homeowners during busy stretches. With Leaping AI calling real-time leads, they reach homeowners within 10 seconds of the lead coming in. They booked 3 appointments on day one and now average 4 to 10 appointments a day.[Thompson Creek](https://leapingai.com/customers/home-services-thompson-creek) brought their speed to lead down to 7 seconds and scheduled close to $100,000 in appointments within 2 days of launch.


## **One call isn't follow-up**


While speed can get you some conversations, it won’t get you every appointment. Plenty of homeowners don’t pick up the phone on the first try, and that’s how leads you’ve paid for end up dying in the CRM.


Most dialing tools are designed to quickly get to that first call. It is the second, third, or fourth attempt at contact where things fall apart.[Independent Home](https://leapingai.com/customers/independent-home-aged-lead-reactivation) , a nationwide bathroom remodeler, ran into just that challenge. Their old dialer was fast on fresh leads but couldn't keep working a lead past the first attempt.


This is what Leaping AI’s Campaigns feature is built for. A campaign works one lead over days with a mix of calls and texts, then stops the moment the homeowner picks up the phone, calls back, or replies to a text. Each new lead gets worked automatically, so none of the leads you paid for sit untouched.


For companies like Direct Remodels, that means 100 touch points over 30 days on every lead. Calls and texts are spaced out inside your contact hours, personalized with the details in your CRM, and they always skip numbers on the Do Not Call list. No lead gets abandoned after a single touch.


It’s not a good use of a CSR’s time to make dozens of touches per lead, by hand. That’s where AI can bring efficiency and scale to the call center, leaving humans to do the more valuable work only they can do.


## **AI and your team, not AI instead of your team**


The next worry that leads call center leaders to play it safe with AI agents is, will this tool convert leads as well as your reps?


On a single call, your reps might perform better than the AI. That’s fine. But it’s not the comparison you should be analyzing. Your reps can’t be first on every single lead. They can’t make the fifth attempt to text every contact that came in three days ago. They can’t be on the phones at 7pm on a Sunday. The better question you should be asking is whether AI *plus* your team books more appointments than the human CSRs alone.


The only way this marriage of humans and AI works is if your team stays in the loop:


-


**Your CSRs work in the same tool.** They see every call recording, transcript, and text thread, lead by lead.


-


**Dropped calls get picked up fast.** When a call drops, your team gets notified by email so a rep can call the homeowner right back.


-


**Your best people move to higher-value work.** At Lifetime Bath & Glass, the AI took over enough routine calling that their top-performing CSR was promoted to customer success manager. At Panda Exteriors, five CSRs moved from scheduling calls to outbound telemarketing.


As[Panda Exteriors](https://leapingai.com/customers/appointment-booking-with-voice-ai-panda) CEO Christian Curry put it: "We repurposed five CSRs to outbound telemarketing and lowered our CAC by 3%."


## **What this looks like in practice**


We recently sat down with the CEO and call center manager of a home improvement company that had been using Leaping AI on aged leads, about two weeks old. They weren't happy, since the AI wasn't setting as many appointments as they'd hoped.


Every time we'd suggested letting the AI agent work real-time leads, the answer was the same. "We want to test old leads first."


So we walked them through Campaigns. We showed them how a new lead gets a text the moment it arrives, two calls right behind it, and then 100 touch points over 30 days until the homeowner connects. We showed them how their call center would see every call and get alerts on dropped calls.


They decided to make the jump. Leaping AI is now working all of their real-time lead aggregator leads for two months, and our team and theirs are reviewing appointment numbers together.


Nothing about the product changed between those two conversations. What changed was which leads it was given.


## **Where aged leads still belong**


None of this means you should stop working aged leads. They are often the cheapest appointments you’ll ever book because you already paid for the lead.


Independent Home put Leaping AI on their aged and dormant leads, and years-old leads are now turning into appointments and sales. As CEO Yale Lipschik said: "Our old dialer couldn't call old leads. They'd just be out there to die. Now we're reviving them and turning them into appointments and sales."


[Bath Experts](https://leapingai.com/customers/bath-experts-outbound-voice-ai) runs both newer and aged leads. "Leaping AI helps us to systematically contact our real-time and aged leads lists and is booking us on average five incremental appointments a day," said Jay Shah, Head of Marketing.


Aged lead reactivation is a strong second play once real-time leads are running and you’ve ensured all new leads are being worked as soon as they come in. Campaigns can work an aged lead for up to 85 days of calls and texts. Judge it by the appointments it adds on top of what your team was already booking, and not by how it compares to fresh leads.


## **How to run a fair test**


The last worry is the most honest one. "I don't want to set fewer appointments than we do today." Neither do we. A good pilot is built so you'll know the results quickly, with your own numbers.


1.


**Start with real-time leads.** Pick a lead source with steady volume, like a lead aggregator or your web form, and send every new lead to voice AI as it comes in.


2.


**Set a timeframe.** Give it long enough to see a full follow-up cycle play out. The company in the story above chose two months. Look at your sales cycle and choose an amount of time that will let you see the full picture.


3.


**Build the campaign around your contact policy.** Set your contact hours and days, how many touches, and when a lead stops: on connect, on callback, or on a text reply.


4.


**Keep your team in the tool.** Your CSRs should be watching calls, handling dropped-call alerts, and calling back fast.


5.


**Agree on the scorecard up front.** Track appointments set and appointments held, side by side with what that lead source produced before. Review it together on a regular schedule.


6.


**Add aged leads after.** Once real-time is running, set up a second campaign for your aged list.


If the appointments aren't there, you'll see it. If they are, you'll have the numbers to roll it out across every lead source.
